subject: General Knowledge
topic: First Women of India — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Which officer became the first woman to be inducted into the Indian Police Service (IPS) in 1972?

options.option_text: Kanchan Chaudhary Bhattacharya, first woman DGP in Uttarakhand
Kiran Bedi, who later reformed Tihar Jail as its Inspector General
Archana Ramasundaram, first woman to head a central paramilitary force
Meeran Chadha Borwankar, who served as Commissioner in Pune Police

questions.explanation: Kiran Bedi was inducted into the IPS in 1972, becoming the first Indian woman IPS officer. She is widely remembered for her work as Inspector General of Tihar Jail (1993). Kanchan Chaudhary Bhattacharya is a common confusion — she joined the IPS later and became the first woman DGP (Uttarakhand, 2004), not the first IPS inductee.

questions.stem: Who was sworn in as the first woman Speaker of the Indian Lok Sabha in 2009, presiding over the 15th Lok Sabha?

options.option_text: Sumitra Mahajan, who served as Lok Sabha Speaker during 2014 to 2019
Meira Kumar, first woman elected to the office of Lok Sabha Speaker
Sushma Swaraj, who served as Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha
Sonia Gandhi, President of INC and leader of the United Progressive Alliance

questions.explanation: Meira Kumar was elected Speaker of the 15th Lok Sabha in 2009, making her the first woman to hold this constitutional position. Sumitra Mahajan became the second woman Speaker in 2014 — a frequent exam trap. Sushma Swaraj served as Leader of Opposition, not Speaker.

questions.stem: Which Bengali author won the Jnanpith Award in 1976, becoming the first woman to receive India's highest literary honour?

options.option_text: Amrita Pritam, acclaimed Punjabi poet who won the Jnanpith Award in 1981
Mahasweta Devi, activist-author celebrated for Hajar Churashir Maa
Ashapurna Devi, author of Pratham Pratishruti anchoring the Subarnarekha trilogy
Nabaneeta Dev Sen, Bengali feminist author and Sahitya Akademi awardee

questions.explanation: Ashapurna Devi won the Jnanpith Award in 1976 for her novel Pratham Pratishruti — making her the first woman Jnanpith laureate. Amrita Pritam is the most tempting distractor because she also won the Jnanpith, but in 1981 (the second woman). Mahasweta Devi won in 1996.

questions.stem: Which Indian athlete won a bronze medal at the 2000 Sydney Olympics, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?

options.option_text: P. T. Usha, sprint legend who narrowly missed bronze at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics
Karnam Malleswari, who won bronze in the 69 kg weightlifting event at Sydney
Kunjarani Devi, multiple world champion in weightlifting from Manipur
Mary Kom, five-time world boxing champion who won bronze at London 2012

questions.explanation: Karnam Malleswari won bronze in the 69 kg weightlifting category at Sydney 2000, the first Olympic medal ever won by an Indian woman. P. T. Usha is the classic distractor — she famously finished 4th at 1984 Los Angeles, missing bronze by a fraction of a second. Mary Kom's medal came 12 years later at London 2012.

questions.stem: Justice Leila Seth became the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court in India in 1991. Which High Court did she head as Chief Justice?

options.option_text: Delhi High Court, where she had earlier served as a judge
Allahabad High Court, the largest High Court in India
Himachal Pradesh High Court, with its seat in Shimla
Bombay High Court, one of the oldest High Courts in India

questions.explanation: Justice Leila Seth was appointed Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court in 1991, becoming the first woman to head any High Court in India. Delhi High Court is the most tempting distractor because she had previously served as a judge there — but she was never its Chief Justice.

questions.stem: Which woman earned India's first female pilot's licence in 1936, flying a Gypsy Moth biplane from the Lahore Flying Club at just 21 years of age?

options.option_text: Durba Banerjee, who later became India's first woman airline pilot in the 1950s
Sarla Thakral, who received her A-licence and flew over undivided Punjab
Harita Kaur Deol, first Indian Air Force woman to complete a solo flight
Prem Mathur, first woman to obtain a commercial pilot's licence post-1947

questions.explanation: Sarla Thakral obtained India's first female pilot's A-licence in 1936 at age 21 from the Lahore Flying Club. Durba Banerjee is a strong distractor — she became the first woman commercial airline pilot (Indian Airlines, 1950s), a later and different milestone. Harita Kaur Deol flew her IAF solo sortie in 1994.

questions.stem: India's first winner of the Miss World title later qualified as a medical doctor at the Royal College of Surgeons. Who won this crown in 1966, becoming the first Indian and first Asian to do so?

options.option_text: Sushmita Sen, the first Indian to win the Miss Universe title in 1994
Reita Faria, first Indian and first Asian woman to win the Miss World crown
Nafisa Joseph, Miss India and popular MTV anchor in the late 1990s
Yukta Mookhey, who won the Miss World title representing India in 1999

questions.explanation: Reita Faria won the Miss World crown in 1966 — the first Indian and first Asian to win it — and subsequently qualified as a doctor from the Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland. Aishwarya Rai (1994) and Yukta Mookhey (1999) won later. Sushmita Sen is the sharpest distractor: she won Miss Universe 1994, not Miss World, and many candidates conflate the two titles.
